newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Ugandan coffee crop seen up 50 pct in next few yrs.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan coffee crop seen up 50 pct in next few yrs.

text.p: A top Ugandan government official said on Thursday he expects the Ugandan coffee crop to increase to six million 60-kg bags in the next few years from the current production of 4 million bags.

"I anticipate in the next two (crop) years we are looking at six million bags of robusta coffee," Rwendeire Abel, minister of state for trade and industry, which is responsible for coffee, told Reuters at a tea and coffee symposium in Vienna.
He said the Ugandan coffee authorities were also striving to increase its small arabica production, which currently makes up some 10 percent of total coffee output.
Abel said total coffee output for the 96/97 crop (September to August) was expected to drop to four million bags from the previous season's production of 4.3 million, in part due to a drought.

Uganda plans to increase its production area from the current 270,000 hectares to about 300,000 hectares of coffee plantations over the next few years. -- Maja Wallengren, Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12256
